scenes.title: Course Handbook and Study Guide
scenes.narration: Cardiac arrest is the only emergency in which the actions of the nearest person, in the first three minutes, matter more than everything done by everyone else afterwards. This course is built around that fact. This handbook explains how the course is organised, how you are assessed, and what the course can and cannot certify.

The course is issued as eleven modules, in separate documents, so that departments can assign what each role needs. The first five modules form the core. They take 1.0 hour each, and they are for every clinical staff member. Modules 6 to 11 carry the advanced life support, peri-arrest, post-arrest and systems content, at 1.25 hours each, for those who respond to or lead codes.
rows: Those who respond to or lead codes

scenes.narration: In total, the course lasts 13 hours. Approximately 9 hours are self-paced module study, 2.5 hours are applied practice and scenario work, and 1.5 hours are assessment. This is in addition to the hands-on provider course and skills assessment that basic or advanced life support certification requires. These hours are MedSkills recommended durations. Your hospital's resuscitation policy sets the certification and recertification interval, and that is binding.

notes.note: Your hospital's policy sets the recertification interval

scenes.narration: If you trained on the 2020 guidelines, most of what you know remains correct. You are updating, not relearning. The compression rate of 100 to 120 per minute still holds, as does the 30 to 2 ratio for single-rescuer adult cardiopulmonary resuscitation. The reversible causes, and the overall shape of the algorithms, are also unchanged.

What changed matters, though. There is now a single unified Chain of Survival covering adults and children, in hospital and out of hospital. The terminology has been revised. Rescue breaths is no longer used; breaths now refers to assisted breathing, and ventilation is reserved for mechanical respiratory support. Opioid antagonists have entered the basic life support algorithm for healthcare professionals, and there is a new choking algorithm. In shockable rhythms, epinephrine now follows initial defibrillation attempts that have failed, rather than being given alongside them. Vasopressin is no longer recommended as a substitute for epinephrine.
rows: One chain: adults and children, in and out of hospital
Added to the BLS algorithm for healthcare professionals

scenes.narration: You study the modules in order. Each carries a knowledge check written in the style of the final assessment, so attempt every check before reading the answers. The final assessment covers all eleven modules, and your institution sets the pass mark and the permitted attempts. If you pass, a verifiable MedSkills certificate of knowledge completion is issued, with date and duration written to your training record. It records knowledge, not psychomotor skill. Compressions, bag-mask ventilation and defibrillator operation must be assessed physically at an authorised training centre, so your provider card comes only from a hands-on course.

scenes.narration: By the end of the course you should be able to recognise cardiac arrest within seconds, and start compressions without waiting for permission or for the team. You should describe high-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation precisely, with its rate, depth, recoil and interruptions, and explain why each parameter matters. You should operate a defibrillator and describe safe manual defibrillation, including pad placement and keeping the pause around each shock short. And you should deliver the immediate bundle after return of spontaneous circulation, understanding the harm of too much oxygen and of overbreathing.

points.note: Within seconds, then start compressions without waiting

points.label: Defibrillate
points.note: Pad placement; minimise the peri-shock pause

scenes.narration: Read the modules in order, because each builds on the previous one. Attempt every knowledge check before you read the answers. Print the algorithm figures and post them beside the resuscitation trolley. Skills decay within months, so brief, frequent practice beats a long course every two years. Finally, drug doses, energy settings and targets must be checked against your own hospital's resuscitation policy. Where the hospital protocol differs from this material, follow the hospital protocol and raise the discrepancy with your resuscitation committee.

scenes.narration: Remember three things. The nearest person acts first, so start compressions at once. This is a knowledge course: it builds the reasoning behind each step, but it does not replace hands-on training, and it does not confer an American Heart Association, European Resuscitation Council or equivalent provider card. And always check every dose and setting against your hospital's own policy.
